---
title: "9. Alignment of relative data measurements"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4, dpi = 96,
                      fig.retina = 2, message = FALSE)
inWords <- function(n) if (n %in% 1:12) c("one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven",
  "eight", "nine", "ten", "eleven", "twelve")[n] else format(n)
source("results/stored.R")
# through do.call: the resource scan of rmarkdown purls the article elsewhere and runs
# every literal read_chunk() call there
do.call(knitr::read_chunk, list(file.path("results", "guide-alignment.R")))
saved <- stored("results/guide-alignment.rds", "results/guide-alignment.R", envir = new.env())
```

Western blots, plate readers and similar assays read on experiment-specific scales.
`alignmentModel()` and `align()` bring all experiments onto one common scale by maximum likelihood,
with the reading model written as an expression, as in the R package
[blotIt](https://github.com/JetiLab/blotIt).

```{r}
library(dMod2)
library(ggplot2)
options(dMod2.outdir = file.path(tempdir(), "guide-alignment"))
dir.create(getOption("dMod2.outdir"), showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## Simulated blot data

A phosphorylation at five time points, six biological replicates on six gels, every sample in
three lanes. Simulated: 20 % biological variability per sample, exposure and background per gel,
15 % technical noise per lane.

```{r data}
```

## Alignment model

A reading is value `yi` times gel scale `sj` plus background `bj`, with relative error. Each
symbol is a linear predictor over the data columns, on log scale. `technical = "lane"` averages
the lanes of a sample, see
[technical and biological replicates](#technical-and-biological-replicates).

```{r model}
```

The geometric mean of the values is held at 1 within each block of experiments sharing values.

## Fit by restricted likelihood

`align()` fits from several perturbed starts and keeps the best; error parameters by restricted
maximum likelihood. The fits of this chapter are loaded from `results/guide-alignment.rds`,
computed by `results/guide-alignment.R`.

```{r fit, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
fit <- saved$fit
fit
```

Aligned values with standard errors:

```{r}
fit$aligned
```

## Comparison with the simulation

Error (log ratio of aligned to simulated course) against the standard error `se`:

```{r}
simulated <- data.frame(time = times, value = truth / exp(mean(log(truth))))
errors <- function(fit) {
  a <- fit$aligned[match(times, fit$aligned$time), ]
  data.frame(time = times, simulated = simulated$value, aligned = a$value,
             error = log(a$value / simulated$value), se = a$se)
}
signif(errors(fit), 2)
```

```{r, fig.height = 3.5}
ggplot(fit$aligned, aes(time, value)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = value - sigma, ymax = value + sigma), width = 0) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = "aligned")) +
  geom_point(data = simulated, aes(shape = "simulated")) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(aligned = 16, simulated = 4), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "time [min]", y = "value") + theme_dMod2()
```

## Technical and biological replicates

Technical replicates (lanes, wells) measure the same sample and share the biological deviation
of that sample. `technical = "lane"` averages them before the alignment; readings agreeing in all
columns but `value`, `lloq` and the technical columns form one sample. The mean is geometric for a
relative error model, arithmetic for an absolute one. The same data with every lane as a reading:

```{r lanes, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
fitLanes <- saved$lanes
fitLanes
```

```{r}
signif(errors(fitLanes), 2)
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
# the largest error of an aligned value in units of the standard error
inSE <- function(fit) with(errors(fit), max(abs(error / se)))
```

The lane fit reports standard errors smaller by about $\sqrt{3}$; the errors reach
`r round(inSE(fitLanes), 1)` standard errors, those of the fit of means stay within
`r inWords(ceiling(inSE(fit)))`.

## Random background per gel

A random effect per gel around a common background, integrated by FOCEI as in
[Nonlinear mixed-effects models](guide-nlme.html). A prior on `omega_bj_bj`, the log standard
deviation, normal around $\log 0.3$ with standard deviation 0.3:

```{r background, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
fit2 <- saved$background
fit2
```

```{r}
signif(errors(fit2), 2)
```

Background per gel against the simulation:

```{r}
bg <- exp(fit2$parameters[["bj"]] + fit2$random$mode[match(gels, fit2$random$group)])
data.frame(gel = gels, simulated = round(background), common = round(exp(fit$parameters[["bj"]])),
           random = round(bg))
```

Values change by less than their standard errors. Bands far above the background leave it
unresolved; gels with weak lanes resolve it, see
[Western blots](#western-blot-and-targeted-mass-spectrometry).

## Fit options

| argument | default | controls |
|---|---|---|
| `fits` | `10` | fits from perturbed starts |
| `sd` | `0.5` | standard deviation of the perturbation |
| `reml` | `TRUE` | error parameters and random-effect spreads by restricted likelihood |
| `method` | `"focei"` | with random terms, `"focei"` or `"quadrature"` |
| `cores` | `1` | fits in parallel |

Fits stop at tolerances of about $10^{-8}$. Absolute readings, such as mass spectrometry
concentrations, are marked in a column `absolute` and fix the scale of their block.

## qPCR with censored wells

Target mRNA at seven time points in four experiments, each on a subset of time points, every
sample in two wells. 36 - Ct is the log2 concentration in arbitrary units; a well without Ct after
40 cycles lies below -4.

### qPCR data

Column `lloq` holds the limit of each reading; an `NA` reading is censored there. Standard
deviation 0.5 cycles between samples, 0.25 between wells.

```{r qpcrdata}
```

### qPCR model

A reading is `yi + sj`, log2 concentration plus experiment offset, with absolute error.
`technical = "well"` averages the wells; a sample with one well below the limit is censored at the
mean of the other well and the limit.

```{r qpcrmodel}
```

### qPCR fit

The mean of the values is held at 0; `log2fc` is relative to the untreated value.

```{r qpcrfit, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
fit <- saved$qpcr
fit
```

```{r}
a <- fit$aligned
a$log2fc <- a$estimate - a$estimate[a$time == 0]
cbind(a[c("time", "estimate", "se", "log2fc")], simulated = log2fold[match(a$time, times)])
```

Sample means before and after alignment, censored samples not drawn:

```{r}
s <- fit$scaled[!fit$scaled$bloq, ]
both <- rbind(data.frame(s[c("experiment", "time")], stage = "before", value = s$value),
              data.frame(s[c("experiment", "time")], stage = "after", value = s$scaled))
both$stage <- factor(both$stage, c("before", "after"))
```
```{r fig.height = 3.5}
ggplot(both, aes(factor(time), value, color = experiment)) +
  geom_point() + facet_wrap(~ stage) +
  labs(x = "time [h]", y = "log2(conc.) [a.u.]", color = "experiment") +
  scale_color_dMod2() + theme_dMod2()

```
```{r fig.height = 3.5}
plotAligned(fit) + scale_x_sqrt(breaks = times) + labs(x = "time [h]", y = "log2(conc.) [a.u.]")
```
```{r fig.height = 3}
plotResiduals(fit)
```

### Aligned values as data

```{r}
as.datalist(fit)
```

## Western blot and targeted mass spectrometry

A phosphoprotein on ten gels, five with a short course up to 4 h and five with a long one up to
48 h, sharing the untreated lane and 4 h, and by targeted mass spectrometry in nM at four time
points. The background per gel is a normal random effect. Mass spectrometry readings are marked in
column `absolute`, predicted by the expression `absolute` (by default the first biological symbol)
and have gel `NA`; the block comes out in nM.

### Blot and mass spectrometry data

Log2 band in arbitrary units or log2 concentration in nM; gels S1 to S5 short, L1 to L5 long.

```{r wbdata}
```

### Blot and mass spectrometry model

A band reads `log2(2^yi + 2^(b + bj)) + sj`, a mass spectrometry reading `yi`, with absolute
error per method. Priors: `omega_bj_bj` normal around $\log 0.3$ with standard deviation 0.3, `b`
normal around 0 with standard deviation 2.

```{r wbmodel}
```

### Blot and mass spectrometry fit

Values in log2 nM, also at time points without mass spectrometry:

```{r wbfit, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
fit <- saved$wb
fit
```

```{r}
a <- fit$aligned[order(fit$aligned$time), ]
cbind(a[c("time", "estimate", "se")], nM = round(2^a$estimate, 1), simulated = conc[match(a$time, times)])
```

Background in nM and standard deviations of both methods on log2 scale:

```{r}
p <- fit$parameters
round(2^p[["b"]], 2)
c(MS = exp(p[["sigma"]]), WB = exp(p[["sigma"]] + p[["sigma_methodWB"]]))
```

Readings before and after alignment; absolute readings stay unchanged:

```{r}
s <- fit$scaled
s$gel <- factor(ifelse(s$absolute, "MS", s$gel), c(gels, "MS"))
panel <- c("before: WB [a.u.]", "before: MS [nM]", "after [nM]")
both <- rbind(data.frame(s[c("gel", "method", "time")], reading = s$value,
                         panel = ifelse(s$absolute, panel[2], panel[1])),
              data.frame(s[c("gel", "method", "time")], reading = s$scaled, panel = panel[3]))
both$panel <- factor(both$panel, panel)
```
```{r fig.height = 4.5}
ggplot(both[is.finite(both$reading), ], aes(factor(time), reading, color = gel, shape = method)) +
  geom_point() + facet_wrap(~ panel, scales = "free_y") +
  guides(x = guide_axis(angle = 45)) +
  labs(x = "time [min]", y = "log2(conc.)", color = "gel", shape = "method") +
  scale_color_dMod2(palette = "dMod") + theme_dMod2() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")

```
```{r fig.height = 3.5}
plotAligned(fit) + scale_x_sqrt(breaks = times) + guides(x = guide_axis(angle = 45)) +
  labs(x = "time [min]", y = "log2(conc.) [nM]")
```
```{r fig.height = 3}
plotResiduals(fit)
```

### Random background

Standard deviation of the log2 background between gels, and per gel the mode with conditional
standard error:

```{r}
fit$omega
fit$random
```

Shrinkage $1 - \operatorname{SD}(\text{modes}) / \omega$; aligned values, `b` and $\omega$ do
not depend on the modes.

```{r}
fit$fit$shrinkage
```

Conditional draws against the estimated normal:

```{r fig.height = 5}
plotRandomEffects(fit$fit)
```

Individual (IPRED) and population prediction (PRED):

```{r fig.height = 3.5}
plot(fit$fit) + theme(legend.position = "right") + labs(color = "gel")
```

Reference: `alignmentModel()`, `align()`, `plotAligned()`, `plotResiduals()`, `plotRandomEffects()`
